Amazon VPC

Amazon VPC is the private network boundary where AWS workloads receive IP space, subnets, routing and network security controls.

Architecture / mental model

VPC CIDR
├─ public/private subnets across AZs
├─ route tables
├─ gateways/endpoints
└─ Security Groups + Network ACLs

How it works

A VPC is a logically isolated virtual network in AWS. CIDR ranges define the address space from which subnet ranges are carved, and those subnets place resources into Availability Zones.

Routing decides how traffic leaves a subnet; gateways and endpoints provide paths to the internet, private AWS services or other networks; Security Groups and NACLs control different filtering boundaries.

The original finalized Day 6 wording framed VPC as 'Building Your Own Private Network' and connected CIDR, subnets, route tables, internet access and security boundaries. That remains the right mental model: the VPC is the network canvas, not merely one resource in a list.

Hands-on reference

aws ec2 describe-vpcs
aws ec2 describe-subnets
aws ec2 describe-route-tables

Verification

Choose one VPC and trace its CIDR, subnets, route-table associations, gateways/endpoints and Security Groups. If you cannot sketch the path for a packet, the VPC is not yet understood.

Field note / gotcha

A resource being 'inside a VPC' does not automatically make it private. Subnet routes, public addressing and attached services determine actual reachability.

Security considerations

Plan address space before growth, separate public and private tiers intentionally and keep east-west access controlled instead of treating everything inside the VPC as trusted.

What I learned

Cloud networking becomes understandable when every resource is placed on an explicit address, routing and trust map.
